source.title: On Generalization of Adaptive Methods for Over-parameterized Linear Regression
source.authors: Vatsal Shah; S. Basu; Anastasios Kyrillidis; S. Sanghavi

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study plots test error over training iterations in an over-parameterized linear-regression experiment, using an adaptive-method setting rather than the original model-size sweep. Its text identifies a double-descent-like pattern in estimation error, not test error.
record.gate_note: The paper's double-descent background discussion cites other work and is not a result row. Figure 2 plots test error and estimation error over iterations; only the estimation-error pattern is explicitly described as double-descent-like. Deep-learning test-accuracy plots are generalization results, but the text does not identify a double-descent shape in them.
record.test_reason: The paper studies how adaptive optimizers generalize in over-parameterized linear regression and deep networks. It does not test any version of double descent. Double descent appears only as background (cited) and as one passing remark: Figure 2's caption says AM2's estimation error ||w(t)−w*|| over iterations is plotted semilog 'to highlight the double descent like phenomena'. That curve is figure-only and measures parameter estimation error, not test error. The authors' own theory (Remark on Dynamics) predicts in-span error decaying while out-of-span error rises and saturates, a fall-then-rise-to-plateau rather than a fall-rise-fall. The Figure 2 test-error curves (r1–r4) are never described in shape, and no numbers are given. No model-size, sample-size, noise or regularization sweep bears on V1 or V3–V7. No verdict can be drawn.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly correct. The authors' main conclusion is that whether an adaptive method matches SGD's minimum-norm solution and generalization depends on whether the preconditioner stays in the data span (Theorem 1 conditions), plus initialization and data. In deep nets there is no clear winner and tuning matters. Double descent is only a side remark about AM2's estimation error, not a claim about test-error curves.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares adaptive and non-adaptive optimization methods in over-parameterized regression and neural networks; it does not reproduce the original model-size, sample-size, or test-error double-descent experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that outcomes vary with optimizer, problem/data, architecture, and hyperparameter configuration; it does not establish these as dependencies of a test-error double-descent peak.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2's caption describes AM2 (squared-diagonal Adagrad variant) estimation error ||w(t)−w*|| over iterations as 'double descent like'. Theory predicts the out-of-span error rises and saturates while the in-span error decays.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In unregularized over-parameterized linear regression, some adaptive preconditioners give a non-monotone parameter-error trajectory over iterations, driven by out-of-span drift.

record.problems: The relevant curves are presented only in plots, without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The explicit double-descent-like description is for estimation error, not test error.
record.rows_left_out: Deep-learning test-accuracy curves are shown in Figures 3 and 4, but the text does not describe a double-descent shape in them; they are not extracted as test-error double-descent results. No model-size or sample-size sweeps are reported.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep. M1-UP/OP and C1-UP/OP compare two sizes only by optimizer accuracy and show no peak.
No readable epoch-wise fall-rise-fall in test error, in either the linear-regression or the deep-network curves (Figs 2–4).
n=10 vs n=40 at d=50 (Table 3) shows test error falling with more data, but this is not a sweep near the interpolation threshold.
Noise and regularization are not varied with respect to a peak. The ℓ2-regularized case is analyzed only theoretically, as convergence to a unique solution.

record.verdict_notes: In isotropic Gaussian linear regression, expected test MSE equals ||w−w*||^2 plus noise, so r5 is a near-proxy for test risk. Even so, the remark is unquantified, rests on a log-x figure, and the theory describes rise-and-plateau rather than a second descent. It should not be counted as evidence for V2. The Table 1/3 n=10 vs n=40 comparison is not a V3 test.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error curve around a size interpolation threshold.

The text does not explicitly establish fall-rise-fall in test error; the explicit double-descent-like observation concerns estimation error. No epoch-wise double-descent result for deep networks is stated.
No comparison of sample sizes near an interpolation threshold for test error.
No capacity sweep testing a general double-descent curve across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak locations.
Noise levels and regularization are not varied to test peak causes, multiple peaks, or disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
No alternative parameter-count measure is used to test whether the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.
